content.value_statement: Azure authentication in .NET apps can be confusing across local and production environments. This skill provides practical patterns for credential chains, managed identity, service principals, and SDK clients.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation commands for Azure.Identity and related .NET packages.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential order and common customization options.
Provides examples for managed identity, service principals, and developer credentials.
Demonstrates Azure SDK client setup with Blob Storage and Key Vault examples.
Summarizes error handling, retry options, logging, and credential reuse guidance.
limitations: It is a documentation skill and does not validate Azure tenant configuration.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted before production use.
It does not create Azure resources, roles, identities, or access policies.
Listed package versions can become stale as Azure SDK releases change.

use_cases.title: Set up local Azure SDK authentication
use_cases.description: Use DefaultAzureCredential with local developer credentials before deploying to Azure.

use_cases.title: Prepare production managed identity
use_cases.description: Select ManagedIdentityCredential patterns for Azure-hosted services without storing client secrets.

use_cases.title: Review credential choices
use_cases.description: Compare service principal, developer, user, and workload identity options for a .NET application.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a starting credential
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new .NET Azure SDK project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an Azure Identity credential for a new .NET app. I need local development and Azure deployment support.

prompt_templates.title: Add DefaultAzureCredential
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic implementation with an Azure SDK client.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to use DefaultAzureCredential with an Azure SDK client in .NET. Explain what I should replace for my environment.

prompt_templates.title: Design production authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Production deployment that should avoid stored secrets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Azure Identity approach for my .NET service using managed identity. Include local development and deployment differences.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a credential chain
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing authentication design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my .NET Azure authentication plan. Identify weak credential choices, environment variable risks, and safer Azure Identity alternatives.

output_examples.input: I need authentication for a .NET API running in Azure App Service and on developer laptops.
output_examples.output: Recommended plan: use DefaultAzureCredential locally and ManagedIdentityCredential in production. Assign the managed identity only the required Azure roles.

output_examples.input: My app uses a client secret today. I want a safer Azure-hosted option.
output_examples.output: Suggested migration: replace the service principal secret with managed identity where supported. Keep service principal credentials only for external hosting cases.

output_examples.input: I need to understand why authentication fails in my .NET Azure SDK client.
output_examples.output: Expected guidance: check credential availability, tenant settings, role assignments, authority host, and Azure Identity exception types.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity for Azure-hosted production workloads.
Use deterministic credentials in production instead of broad developer credential chains.
Reuse credential instances across Azure SDK clients when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not commit tenant IDs, client IDs, secrets, or certificate passwords as real values.
Do not enable interactive browser authentication for unattended production services.
Do not rely on developer CLI credentials in deployed workloads.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Identity authentication patterns for .NET applications using Microsoft Entra ID.

faq.question: Does it execute Azure commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation examples and installation commands that users must choose to run.

faq.question: Can it replace Azure security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps with implementation choices, but access policy and role assignment reviews are still required.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is DefaultAzureCredential always best for production?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends deterministic credentials, such as managed identity, for production workloads.

faq.question: Does it include real credentials?
faq.answer: No. The credential values shown in SKILL.md are placeholders for user-specific configuration.
